title: Fundamentals of Travel Agency and Tour Operation Business (Module 6A, lesson 20)
summary: A travel agency is a business that arranges people's holidays and journeys by booking tickets, hotels and allied facilities. It is a retailer between suppliers (airlines, hotels, car rentals) and tourists and earns mainly through commission. Both travel agencies and tour operators are intermediaries who bring together clients and principal service providers.

Thomas Cook was the first organised travel agent in the world: his first excursion was in 1841 (570 people by train from Leicester to Loughborough); in 1851 he took 16,500 people to the Crystal Palace; he created the inclusive tour (paid in advance) and the Circular Note (1873), forerunner of the traveller's cheque. His son John Mason Cook came to India in 1880 and set up offices in Bombay and Calcutta (India operation from 1881).

A retail travel agency sells tourist products directly to tourists on behalf of suppliers, earning commission and mark-up (the difference between retail price and wholesale cost). It quotes fares, makes reservations, arranges tickets, accommodation, insurance, foreign currency and documents and accepts payments. A wholesale travel agency buys service components in bulk, designs packages and sells them through retailers (or its own outlets); it earns through volume discounts, not commission, and bears market risk since it blocks seats and rooms in advance.

A tour operator buys travel services in volume, assembles them into packages with its own price tag and sells directly or via retailers; it is wholly responsible for delivering the services and is called a manufacturer of package tours. Types: inbound (handle foreign tourists in the host country; 'image builders' that earn foreign exchange; e.g. XYZ Travels handling a French group), outbound (sell tours abroad to people of their own country; arrange documents and contract inbound or ground operators; e.g. XYZ India sending a group to Singapore), domestic (within the home country; e.g. a pilgrimage package from Southern Travels to Amarnath) and ground handlers (also reception operators or destination management companies who provide land arrangements: transport, guides, events, car rentals).

Tour operator: a wholesaler, creates new products and packages, located in mega cities, has large size and multi-service capacity, handles ground services and foreign currency. Retail agency: sells packages on behalf of the wholesaler, an intermediary, follows the itinerary, works on commission, can be located anywhere. Wholesale agency: does not sell to clients directly, buys in bulk and assembles packages, smaller scale and operations. An online travel agency (OTA) works on the internet through a global distribution system and offers information, bookings, packages and online payment.

objective: Identify True or False. (a) A person goes to France from India and buys a tour package from ABC India, who do all the travel document processing; ABC India is an outbound tour operator. (b) There are three types of travel agencies.
(a) True. (b) False: there are two, retail and wholesale.

vsa: Explain the meaning of a travel agency.
A travel agency is a business that arranges holidays and journeys by booking tickets, hotels and allied facilities. It acts as a retailer between the supplier and the tourist.
What is meant by a mark-up price?
It is the price obtained by marking up the cost of a tour and selling it at a higher price. The difference between the retail price and the wholesale cost is the mark-up.
Who is a ground operator? State two ground services.
A ground operator, also called a reception or destination management company, provides land arrangements at a destination. Services include local transport, guides and car rentals.
Why are travel agencies and tour operators called intermediaries?
They bring together clients and the principal service providers. They strengthen the selling and buying process for both the customer and the hotels or airlines.
sa: Explain any three functions of a travel agency.

(i) It quotes fares and rates and makes reservations for air, rail and hotel. (ii) It arranges tickets, accommodation, travel insurance, foreign currency and documents. (iii) It accepts payments and acts as a single contact for the tourist.
Distinguish between a retail travel agency and a wholesale travel agency with an example.

(i) A retail agency sells packages directly to tourists and earns commission; a wholesale agency buys in bulk and does not sell directly. (ii) A retail agency works on commission and mark-up; a wholesale agency earns through discounts on bulk reservations. (iii) For example, a local agency booking a Goa trip is a retailer while a firm that blocks hotel rooms and flight seats to make packages is a wholesaler.
Explain any three functions of the outbound tour operators.

(i) They sell package tours to people of their own country for foreign destinations. (ii) They arrange travel documents and transportation to the starting point. (iii) They contract inbound or ground operators for accommodation, sightseeing and services abroad.
Explain any three functions of a wholesale travel agency.

(i) It buys travel components in bulk from suppliers. (ii) It designs and assembles package tours. (iii) It sells packages through retail agents and provides consultancy, visa documents and currency exchange.
la: Who are inbound, outbound, domestic and ground operators? Explain with examples.

(i) Inbound operators handle foreign tourists in the host country; a French group handled by XYZ Travels in India. (ii) They are image builders and earn foreign exchange. (iii) Outbound operators send people of their country abroad, arranging documents; XYZ India sending a group to Singapore. (iv) Domestic operators work within the home country; Southern Travels' pilgrimage package for Chennai tourists to Amarnath. (v) Ground operators, also called reception operators or destination management companies, provide land arrangements. (vi) They provide transport, guides, events and accommodation where large companies have no local office.
Differentiate between a tour operator, a retail travel agency and a wholesale travel agency, in six points.

(i) A tour operator is a wholesaler that creates its own packages; a retail agency sells on behalf of the wholesaler. (ii) A wholesale agency buys in bulk and does not sell to clients directly. (iii) A tour operator is based in mega cities; a retail agency can be anywhere. (iv) A tour operator is more inclined to ground handling; wholesale agencies are less so. (v) A retail agency works on commission; wholesalers earn on volume discounts. (vi) The size and multi-service capacity of a tour operator is high; of a wholesaler it is low.
